scope: Nine remaining Onagraceae inventory records; source-backed research only; no edits to source species.json, photo rights, gallery, BONAP target decisions

references.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
Flora of North America, Vol 10 Onagraceae
Kew Plants of the World Online

records.name: Oenothera calcicola

flora.original_name: Gaura calcicola P.H.Raven & D.P.Greg. (historical synonym; not asserted as a flora treatment)

other.name: Flora of North America vol.10, Oenothera calcicola

characters.habit: Perennial from woody rootstock; stems erect and branched near ground and inflorescence, (40–)60–250 cm
characters.flowers: Four-merous, bilaterally symmetrical, open near sunset; tube 3–9 mm, sepals 6–12 mm, petals 7–11 mm white aging dark pink to red; stigma extends beyond anthers
characters.fruit: Narrow, angled or winged gaura-like capsule; quantitative measurements not transcribed from accessible excerpt
characters.habitat: Mostly limestone/gypsum or calcareous upland; source emphasizes higher-elevation/montane occurrence relative to close taxa

holds: Check full FNA vegetative and mature fruit quantitative description

records.name: Oenothera capillifolia subsp. berlandieri

characters.habit: Bushy, several to many stems, decumbent to ascending, 10–40 cm; annual or perennial in parent species account
characters.leaves: Linear to oblanceolate, nearly entire to finely toothed; largest blades 1–4 cm
characters.flowers: Four-merous yellow, sunrise opening, self-incompatible; hypanthium and stigma yellow, never black; parent account hypanthium 5–16(–20) mm and petals generally 9–21 mm for C. berlandieri
characters.habitat: Dry prairies on sandy, gravelly or limestone soils
characters.diagnosis: Compare former subsp. pinifolius (= current O. capillifolia subsp. capillifolia): taller, less bushy, longer leaves and sometimes black inner tube/stigma

holds: Subspecies phenology from flora region must not be treated as county BONAP evidence

records.name: Oenothera capillifolia

flora.original_name: Calylophus berlandieri Spach sensu lato; 1999 treats subsp. berlandieri and subsp. pinifolius

characters.habit: Annual/short-lived perennial to perennial depending on subspecies; ~10–80 cm across two 1999 treatments
characters.leaves: Linear to oblanceolate; older subsp. berlandieri stem leaves 1–4 cm; older pinifolius 2.5–9 cm
characters.flowers: Four-merous yellow, peltate stigma, eight stamens; hypanthium generally 5–16(–20) mm, angular buds; flowers opening near sunrise
characters.fruit: Cylindric capsule per 1999 Calylophus generic account
characters.phenology: Subsp. berlandieri Mar–Nov; historical pinifolius Mar–Jul; do not collapse this into species-wide exact period
characters.diagnosis: Historical subsp. pinifolius is modern subsp. capillifolia (often erect 30–80 cm; possibly black inner floral tube/stigma); historical subsp. berlandieri is modern same epithet (bushy 10–40 cm, stigma never black)

other.name: FNA Oenothera capillifolia subsp. capillifolia / Kew taxonomic crosswalk

holds: Species-level record and subspecies-level record overlap by design, not two different species
Do not assume both subspecies native in target counties without independent evidence

records.name: Oenothera glaucifolia

characters.habit: Slender, glabrous, brittle-stemmed biennial or perennial 0.6–3 m, infrequently branching below flowering portion
characters.leaves: Sessile, acute, entire, narrowly lanceolate, 3–8(–10) cm long × 4–28 mm
characters.flowers: Four pure-white petals 4–6 mm; eight stamens; panicled terminal spikes
characters.fruit: Single-seeded capsule 2–4 mm long, about 2 mm thick
characters.diagnosis: Unlike strongly zygomorphic former Gaura, 1999 Stenosiphon has evenly arranged white petals, cream anthers, threadlike hypanthium and gradually reduced inflorescence leaves

other.name: Kew POWO Oenothera glaucifolia accepted; Stenosiphon linifolium homotypic synonym

holds: 1999 flora uses Stenosiphon linifolius; Kew spells Stenosiphon linifolium. Retain original spelling as printed and flag epithet discrepancy
1999 life history biennial/perennial vs Kew biennial; inspect FNA

records.name: Oenothera hispida

characters.habit: Rhizomatous perennial forming patches, stems typically several, 0.2–0.6(–1.2) m
characters.flowers: Petals 6–10 mm, pink to red, rarely white (1999 treatment); FNA: white fading red
characters.fruit: Fruits 7–13 mm, abruptly narrowed to cylindrical stipe
characters.diagnosis: Large rhizomatous patches; FNA describes capsule prominently bulging at base of upper pyramidal half versus O. suffrutescens

other.name: FNA Oenothera hispida; synonym Gaura drummondii

holds: Older flora uses pink-to-red petal description vs FNA white fading red; likely age/stage differences, confirm before harmonizing
1999 flora warns earlier misapplication of Gaura odorata

records.name: Oenothera macrocarpa subsp. macrocarpa

characters.habit: Perennial, nearly stemless or suberect/trailing to 0.5 m (species-wide range)
characters.leaves: Subspecies distinguished by greenish, linear-lanceolate to broadly lanceolate blades; gray hairs mainly on youngest tissue
characters.flowers: Species: yellow petals 2–5 cm; tube 5–12 cm; sepals 2–4 cm; opens near sunset
characters.diagnosis: Compared with subsp. incana, less uniformly gray-hairy and generally narrower green leaves; compared with subsp. oklahomensis, not completely glabrous

holds: Measurements come from species treatment unless explicitly marked subspecies

records.name: Oenothera patriciae

characters.habit: Annual to 0.65(–0.85) m; FNA: branched, taprooted, 15–65(–85) cm
characters.leaves: FNA basal rosette lyrate 6–9.5 × 1–2 cm; stem leaves 1–7 × 0.1–2.3 cm, narrow and somewhat toothed
characters.flowers: 1999 hypanthium 6.5–12 mm, petals 8–12.5 mm pink/rose-red or white; FNA white fading pink/purple, floral tube 6–12 mm
characters.fruit: (3–)4-angled, 5.5–10 mm, sessile or stipe 1 mm in 1999; FNA 6–10 × 2–3 mm, deeply furrowed, narrow winging
characters.diagnosis: Buds and sepals pubescent, bracts 2–4 mm, fruits pyramidal broadest at base versus glabrous buds and broader-middle ellipsoid capsules of former Gaura suffulta

holds: Do not confuse historic Gaura brachycarpa Small with distinct Oenothera brachycarpa A.Gray

records.name: Oenothera rosea

other.name: FNA Oenothera rosea; Flora of China species treatment

characters.habit: Rhizomatous or woody-caulescent perennial, ascending to decumbent, 7–65 cm (Flora of China)
characters.leaves: Petioles 3–20 mm; basal blades 2–5 × 0.5–2 cm; stem blades 1–6 × 0.4–2.5 cm, elliptic to oblanceolate, weakly to coarsely toothed
characters.flowers: Near-sunrise opening, rose-purple petals 5–12 mm; floral tube 4–10 mm; sepals 5–10 mm
characters.fruit: Club-shaped to narrowly obovoid capsule 4–12 mm plus slender sterile basal stipe 5–20 mm
characters.habitat: Disturbed moist/creekside weedy areas in cited Flora of China treatment
characters.phenology: May–Nov flowering (Flora of China regional data, not Texas calendar)
characters.diagnosis: Compared with O. speciosa, usually smaller rose-purple petals and narrower club-shaped fruit with long sterile basal stipe

holds: Not found as direct species in 1999 flora; no page asserted
Existing repository target-zone FAIL retained; FNA reports native Mexico / wider southern range, but BONAP county assessment still separate

records.name: Oenothera serrulata

characters.habit: Herb/woody-based perennial or rare annual at genus level; exact individual height not stated in 1999 species account
characters.leaves: Fine-toothed leaves (epithet and family treatment), species measurements require FNA
characters.flowers: Yellow four-merous, eight stamens and peltate stigma (Calylophus genus); self-compatible, open in morning, anthers deposit pollen directly onto stigma
characters.diagnosis: Versus former Calylophus berlandieri: smaller petals normally 6–12 mm, stigma only to inner anthers, substantial aborted pollen 30–80% in 1999 key; parent C. berlandieri petals usually 9–21 mm and pollen 85–100% fertile

historical_synonyms: Oenothera serrulata Nutt. (given in 1999 synonym bracket)

other.name: FNA Oenothera serrulata treatment, broad autogamous complex

holds: FNA character variability broad; do not impose rigid single flower size cutoff
Species name Oenothera serrulata appears in 1999 as synonym, not standalone species heading
